items.title: The derived category of a dg algebra has direct sums and products computed levelwise
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-derived-products at source lines 2894-2904: the derived category of a dg algebra has both direct sums and products, and they are computed by taking the corresponding operations on dg modules. The proof at source lines 2906-2950 is an explicit verification that the levelwise constructions satisfy the universal properties in the derived category. It builds the candidate direct sum of a family of dg modules, checks that it satisfies the universal property up to quasi-isomorphism using the description of morphisms in the derived category supplied by the author's computation of the derived Hom, and then repeats the argument in the opposite direction for products, which requires care with the variance of the constructions and with the fact that a product in the derived category is not simply computed degreewise without accounting for quasi-isomorphisms. Recognising which universal property has to be checked in which category is the substance, and the statement lists only the conclusions.
